title: The Return of Isaiah & The Fall of Arabia

sense.text:
“Now there were in the church that was at Antioch certain prophets and teachers; as Barnabas, and Simeon that was called” Niger. That word right there is Latin and it just means black. They pronounce it a certain way in Egypt today, and they pronounce it Niger so that they don’t offend sensitive black people. Some of you are very sensitive about words, but that is not the pronunciation, and it’s not ‘Niger’ like the country either. With all this talk of ECOWAS wanting to attack Niger over a coup, when most of the ECOWAS presidents got in by a coup themselves, the word matters.

How do we know? Go inside the book Africa’s Gift to America: ‘These first Africans were variously called Niger, from River Niger, Ethiopian’, and Niger was pronounced not Niger, but the way the Southerner said it. I ain’t making nothing up; y’all thought I was being offensive, but I got books to show you how it was pronounced. All of that was to cover up that last word. Don’t be fooled into thinking it was called Niger. When you hear that word everybody knows, and a lot of these old Christians are feeling it through the TV right now. That was the purpose of why they called us that: they wanted us to feel it. Now all of a sudden they act like we’re okay, but in the meantime they treat us like that and tell you you’re all right in Jesus.

This shows how deep Esau’s diabolicalness goes. He wants to quote unquote remove these so-called sensitive words to get you out of the understanding of Deuteronomy 28, the byword and all those bad words they said to us, because those words cause us to see that we’re not getting treated like everybody else and to find out who we are in the Bible. They are trying to wash away our history. That’s the reason they’re taking black history out of school, the CRT and all that: to make us black white people, so to speak, dark on your face but with your whole mind, mentality and history washed.

precepts.why: This is the prophecy, one of the curses God said would be upon our people: “And thou shalt become an astonishment, a proverb, and a byword”. That word called upon Simeon in Acts 13 is one of those bywords; they had the others too, and the proverbs and bywords all mean black. Those are the words, and this is the one we’re focusing on. That is why Esau wants the word pronounced soft and taken out of your mouth: so you never connect it to the byword God said would be upon Israel.

sense.text:
“And the Lord shall scatter thee among all people”: when it says all people, it means all people, “from the one end of the earth even unto the other; and there thou shalt serve other gods, which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, even wood and stone.” When we fell into the Islamic slave trade, we worshiped a stone god called Allah, the Kaaba.

History hardly discusses the Islamic slave trade; we primarily focus on the transatlantic one. A History of the Arab Slave Trade counts 140 million victims, and at least 28 million Africans were enslaved by the Muslims, with at least 80 percent of those captured calculated to have died before reaching the slave market. Do the math: 80 percent of 28 million is 22 million 400 thousand of us dead before we even showed up to the slave markets, and what about the ones after? So don’t tell me about six million people; ours is a true Holocaust. This is to all your Muhammad friends out there in the bodegas: these are their ancestors.

The Arab slave trade lasted more than 13 centuries, from the early 7th century, about 600 A.D., until the 1960s, and in Mauritania slavery was only officially outlawed in August 2007. Islam traces back to 610 A.D., when Muhammad first saw the angel and shared the words of Allah: that is when the Islamic slave trade started, under Muhammad. This is your friendly Arabs. I used to be part of the NOI, but when I learned the truth I felt ashamed and could not follow that no more. Some of the Khazars became Muslims from around 690 to the late 10th century, which is why some Muslims look Caucasian: they are extractions from the Khazars.

It is still going on. December 1st 2017, Time Magazine: men sold at auction in Libya for 400 dollars. ECOWAS rallies its forces to fight Niger, but neither they nor the African Union will rally against Libya or Mauritania for enslaving their own citizens: total hypocrisy. April 17 2023, four months ago: enslavement of African migrants is big business in Libya thanks to European Union funding, crimes against humanity from forced labor and sexual slavery to torture. Big business means there’s no plan to stop it; they’re getting funded to enslave us. Who’s to say the missing young girls aren’t being brought into situations like this? The report says it revived after the NATO-backed operation to depose Muammar Gaddafi, and that was one of the reasons they wanted him gone. And you got black people talking about reparations: as long as one of us is enslaved, none of us are free, because what they do to one of us they can do to all of us. No black Muslim talks about this. You black brothers and sisters that are Sunni and Shiite, none of y’all talk about this; you all need to be ashamed of yourselves, every last one of you. We didn’t want to talk about it, but the men of the Lord are gonna talk about it.

The maps show it. The green lines are the Islamic slave routes, throughout Africa, North Africa the Arabs took over, Yemen, Saudi Arabia, up toward Europe and Spain, over to Iran and Iraq. From the eastern side of Africa, Ethiopia, Kenya, Tanzania, Mozambique, Madagascar, they took the Israelites to Mauritius, Réunion, Pakistan, India, the Bay of Bengal, Sri Lanka. This is Deuteronomy 28:64. These are places our people are at, and brothers, these are places we must eventually venture to go: we need boots on the ground. And that map is microscopic compared to where our people have been scattered to.

The photographs, not drawings, out of Persia and Turkey show it: the black woman a slave to Muslims, that’s how we became Muslims; black boys as slaves behind their owners; a little black girl at the bottom of the stairs, dressed nice but a servant, and when they wanted to rape her later on, they raped her; a tall black brother given as a gift to a little girl, like the girl in Goodbye Uncle Tom who got a slave like a Christmas gift; a slave boy bought as a servant for their children, made to play nice with the baby or else they’d kill him; and they even put us in their military and raised us from children to love and adore them. These were our brothers, Israelites taken from the east coast of Africa, and our people have forgotten about them. Today our people in Islam will fight for that religion, just like black Christians will give their life for white Jesus: the Arabs can do no wrong. Christianity and Islam are the bloodiest religions on the planet Earth. Get mad, suck your teeth, call your mama, call your rock; I don’t care. Share this video with all your Muslim brothers and sisters.

precepts.why:
This is the Kaaba, and the word Kaaba is Arabic for black: the black stone. “As the thief is ashamed when he is found, so is the house of Israel ashamed; they, their kings, their princes, and their priests, and their prophets, Saying to a stock, Thou art my father; and to a stone, Thou hast brought me forth”. We said to a rock, thou hast brought me forth. A stock is a piece of wood, the wood and stone of Deuteronomy 28:64, and that stone is your Kaaba, that’s your Allah.

Muslims will lie and say they don’t worship the rock, they just kiss it. That’s a lie. Their own answer says it: kissing the black stone is an act of worship, in which a Muslim kisses a stone he has no connection to except worshiping Allah by venerating it and following the messenger of Allah. They worship the black rock; that’s what we just read in Jeremiah 2. Millions go there every year, and a storm just hit it last week. It looks like a vulva, if you ask me: you gotta stick your head in there and kiss it. I be rude in speech, but not in knowledge. Come out of Islam; I came out, so can you.

Read it again: “for they have turned their back unto me, and not their face: but in the time of their trouble they will say, Arise, and save us.” How you gonna say to a rock, arise and save us? Impossible. Look at the video of Mecca: they’re crying to a rock to save them.

Pre-Islamic Arabia and Egypt were the end points of the slave circuits out of the Sudan, the land of the blacks, and Somalia. Habashas, the name the Arabs gave the Ethiopians, filled the slave markets of Mecca, and Muhammad accepted slavery as part of the natural order of things. A lot of y’all didn’t realize Mecca was a slave port. My black brothers and sisters in Islam going on a Hajj: that was the largest slave market in the world. This is where we were sold, raped, robbed and murdered, right here in Mecca. Get mad if you want; I don’t give a damn.

Muhammad was no prophet of the Most High God. This dude hated black people; he enslaved us, the children of Israel. The only prophets were of the Israelites: “And I raised up of your sons for prophets, and of your young men for Nazarites. Is it not even thus, O ye children of Israel?” He’s talking about the Israelites, not the Arabs. Only the children of Israel were prophets; the Arabs were never prophets of the Lord, and Muhammad was never a prophet of God.

“They provoked him to jealousy with strange gods, with abominations provoked they him to anger.” The Israelites, our people, provoked the Most High God to jealousy with strange gods. “They sacrificed unto devils, not to God; to gods whom they knew not, to new gods that came newly up”: Allah is a new god that came 610 years after the birth of Christ, a new deity on the planet Earth. These are the gods which neither thou nor thy fathers have known in Deuteronomy 28:64.

“Whom your fathers feared”: our fathers never showed respect or veneration to kissing a rock, kissing a stone, kissing anything called Kaaba or Allah. Are you insane?

Keep the picture on the screen: this is Mecca, the Israelites sitting on the ground in the slave market, black men and black women with chains on their necks in the background.

“They say, If a man put away his wife, and she go from him, and become another man’s, shall he return unto her again? shall not that land be greatly polluted?” It was forbidden for a man to take a wife back if she slept with another man; that was God’s law. Now Jeremiah brings it out in its spiritual context: “but thou hast played the harlot with many lovers”. We played the harlot with many lovers, meaning many gods, many false religions; “yet return again to me, saith the Lord.”

“Lift up thine eyes unto the high places”: many high hills were places of worship. “And see where thou hast not been lien with”: that word means corrupted. “In the ways hast thou sat for them, as the Arabian in the wilderness”. Do you see our sisters sitting for them right there in the ways? We sat for the Arabians in the wilderness, in his slave port. The Bible is prophesying that we would worship false gods under the Arabs.

“And thou hast polluted the land”: in learning Islam we polluted the land, with Islam, the religion of the Arabs; “with thy whoredoms”, the worshiping of rocks and stones, “and with thy wickedness”. Even today you see the Arab invasion still, like the president of one of these countries who went on TV a couple of months ago about the blacks. When we were in Sierra Leone and Uganda we asked the Muslims how they became Muslim, and they said because their parents were Muslim; we asked them to show us prophets in the Quran and they can’t do it.

This is the only book that prophesies our history from start to finish. The Quran don’t even talk about this. There’s no prophecies in the Quran concerning our people, what happened to us and what’s going to happen to us. Challenge them, not in the spirit of hatred but in the spirit of love, because our job is to win the dead Israelites to God’s truth.

sense.text: These were our brothers taken from the east coast of Africa, and our people have forgotten them. Ask a black man on the street and he’ll say those are not his people. We’ve forgotten them, but God has not. “I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel”: that word lost. We lost our culture, our heritage, we lost our freedom; we had already begun to be scattered in slavery.

What are the signs that would follow the Israelites, according to Deuteronomy 28:15 through 68? “Moreover all these curses shall come upon thee, and shall pursue thee, and overtake thee, till thou be destroyed”. Notice the word: curses. The curse of God would pursue us and overtake us; you can’t shake it.

You got scholars, so they call themselves, who really believe economics is the way to escape the curses. Somebody tell Cornel West and people like him, and somebody tell my dear brother Claude Anderson, because he’s a big one on economics: it all sounds good, but economics cannot save us from God’s judgments. Some of you brothers and sisters are well off financially, but the curses still apply to you too.

“Because thou hearkenedst not unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to keep his commandments and his statutes which he commanded thee”. It always goes back to our disobedience of God’s laws. Can somebody tell a Christian that? Can somebody tell a Muslim that?

“And they shall be upon thee for a sign and for a wonder”: they is the curses. The curses would be a sign that identifies who the children of Israel are; whoever these curses fit, those are the children of Israel. “And upon thy seed for ever”: for how long? Forever.

Write this down: the curses involve four things. Number one, slavery. Number two, loss of identity; that’s verse 37. Number three, colonialism. Number four, oppression, forever. Those four things collectively identify who the Israelites are. Put the video of Mecca back up: that slave port, and they are crying to a rock to save them.

The book says the Yoruba Jews claim their ancestors were driven from oasis to oasis by Muslim persecution, not finding rest even when they reached Timbuktu. Go back to Deuteronomy 28: “And among these nations shalt thou find no ease, neither shall the sole of thy foot have rest”. That’s what it says right there in the book: not finding rest even when they reached Timbuktu. “But the LORD shall give thee there a trembling heart, and failing of eyes, and sorrow of mind.”
“In the year that king Uzziah died I saw also the Lord sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up, and his train filled the temple.” His train was the garment.

“Above it stood the seraphims”: the seraphims are angels, high ranking top angels. Their job was to cover the throne. Like the Ark of the Covenant: you had images of angels over the mercy seat, and that was represented from the kingdom of heaven, where the Lord was sitting on the throne and you had the seraphims on either side.

“Each one had six wings; with twain he covered his face, and with twain he covered his feet, and with twain he did fly.” Twain means two.

This is Isaiah speaking before the Lord God: “I am a man of unclean lips, and I dwell in the midst of a people of unclean lips”, talking about the Israelites, a people of unclean lips. “For mine eyes have seen the King, the Lord of hosts”: this King, the Lord of hosts, is Christ. That’s who it’s talking about.

“Having a live coal in his hand, which he had taken with the tongs from off the altar.” The tongs are like when you cook and you pick it up with that, a fork or whatever. The angel came and took out a coal.

“And he laid it upon my mouth”: the angel took the coal and laid it on Isaiah’s mouth, “and said, Lo, this hath touched thy lips; and thine iniquity is taken away, and thy sin purged.” Isaiah’s sin was being purged from him.

“Also I heard the voice of the Lord, saying, Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” The Lord is asking, who can I send back to the earth for us, to teach the world of the Most High. “Then said I, Here am I; send me.” Remember we’re in Isaiah chapter six: this is a prophecy that Isaiah would return. Isaiah said, send me, Lord.

“And he said, Go”: the Lord said to Isaiah, go, “and tell this people, Hear ye indeed, but understand not; and see ye indeed, but perceive not.” He’s talking about the Israelites. This people: we hear the scriptures but we don’t understand; we see what the Bible is saying but we don’t indeed perceive it.

“Make the heart of this people fat, and make their ears heavy, and shut their eyes”: shut their spiritual eyes, “lest they see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and convert, and be healed.”

Look at the church pictures: cobwebs all back there, and blind people in the church. They can’t see it with spiritual eyes, they can’t hear with their spiritual ears, they can’t understand the Bible. Our job is to go tell them, like Christ.

“Then said I, Lord, how long?” How long will this be, Lord? “And he answered, Until the cities be wasted without inhabitant”: until Jerusalem, Israel, is wasted, with no Israelites remaining there; “and the houses without man, and the land be utterly desolate.” He’s talking about 70 A.D. All the Israelites either ran out, got caught in slavery, or were murdered.

precepts.why:
Here’s the precept that Isaiah would return. “Fear not, thou mother of the children: for I have chosen thee, saith the Lord”: the mother is Jerusalem. “For thy help will I send my servants Esau and Jeremy.” Write that down in your Bible: on the computer it’ll say Esau, but that’s wrong. It’s Isaiah.

Ezra was during the Persian captivity. Isaiah had been dead already. God says here, I’m going to send Isaiah and I’m going to send Jeremiah, come back. They don’t know what you’re talking about. What Bible are they reading? Their spiritual eyes must be closed.

“After whose counsel I have sanctified and prepared for thee twelve trees laden with divers fruits”: the twelve trees go back to the twelve apostles, which go with the twelve tribes. So Isaiah and Jeremiah would help them.

Jump back to the chapter before. “I take to witness the grace of the people to come, whose little ones rejoice in gladness”: whose little ones means your children. “And though they have not seen me with bodily eyes”: we’ve not seen the Lord with bodily eyes, “yet in spirit they believe the thing that I say”: in the spirit we believe everything this Bible says.

“And now, brother, behold what glory”, and see the people that come from the east, “Unto whom I will give for leaders, Abraham”: God said, I’m going to send Abraham back. Isaac, I’m going to send Isaac back. Jacob, I’ma send Jacob back. Oseas, that’s Hosea: I’m going to send the prophet Hosea back. Amos, Micheas, the prophet Micah, Joel, Abdias, that’s Obadiah, Jonas, the prophet Jonah, Nahum, Abacuc, the prophet Habakkuk, Sophonias, the prophet Zephaniah, Aggeus, the prophet Haggai, Zachary, the prophet Zechariah, “and Malachy, which is called also an angel of the Lord.”

So the Lord is sending these prophets back in these last days. That’s why they can’t stop this. We don’t know who’s who, but we know those prophets are back. They grew up in a grimy state; now they’re getting their minds right, and they’re going to come to the fulfillment of their spirit. You’ve got to believe that.

Revelation ties into the same thing. “And I heard the number of them which were sealed: and there were sealed an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel.” Guess who’s part of that 144 thousand: Isaiah, Jeremiah, all them names we just read. They’re part of the 144 thousand. They’re coming back.

Christianity is trying to stop this, Islam is trying to stop this. You can’t stop this great awakening.

Watch what he says to the prophet John. This is scripture, Bible, proof that the prophets would be back in these last days. “And I took the little book out of the angel’s hand, and ate it up”: the little book is the Bible. He studied it. “And it was in my mouth sweet as honey”: the Kingdom, that’s the sweetest honey. “And as soon as I had eaten it, my belly was bitter.” You know why it was bitter? Because he saw a lot of death. He saw a lot of brothers and sisters falling off, going back into the world again, and the persecution. That’s the bitterness.

“And he said unto me, Thou must prophesy again before many peoples, and nations, and tongues, and kings.” John died on the island of Patmos. So what you gonna do with that? What in the world does a Christian preacher have to say about this verse? They can’t even read it. There’s no interpretation but what it says; you don’t even have to interpret that.

That’s why it matters when the scriptures talk about loving your neighbor as yourself, and ask how you can say you love God, who you never see, but hate your brother. You might be hating on Father Abraham, Isaac or Jacob. You don’t know who you’re hating on.

Here’s that great awakening of them prophets of the 144 thousand. Like it was said during Men’s Conference, the 144 thousand are all apostles, every last one of them. “And after three days and an half”: after 350 years, “the Spirit of life from God entered into them”. The spirit of life is the Holy Spirit. “And they stood upon their feet; and great fear fell upon them which saw them.” This is what y’all see right now, and it’s nothing to what it’s going to turn into, from state to state, country to country. Mark those words. That’s that fear: they want to shut this down, but it ain’t going to stop nothing.

“Then said he unto me, Prophesy unto the wind, prophesy, son of man, and say to the wind, Thus saith the Lord God; Come from the four winds, O breath”. The breath is the Holy Spirit, the same as the spirit of life from God we just read about in Revelation 11; it’s talking about the same thing. “And breathe upon these slain, that they may live. So I prophesied as he commanded me, and the breath came into them”: the Holy Spirit came into them, “and they lived”: their spirit lived, “and stood up upon their feet, an exceeding great army.” This is the word of God. These are the prophecies that we are living.

Look at the pictures of the brothers. If those men were committing crimes, doing something crazy, every camera would be there. Because of this, they act like they’re not seeing it, and they are struck with terrible fear: who the hell is organizing this? They know it’s the Most High. Like they write in them books: we know this is the Lord dealing with this, but we’re going to tell you it ain’t the Lord, you’re a bunch of fakers. Only the Lord can do something like this. All our lives they told us we were nobody, and now we find ourselves in the greatest movement on planet Earth.

But we should never be satisfied as long as we know our brothers on the other side of the world are being whooped and sold as slaves. We’ve got to go fish them.

Didn’t Christ say the same thing? This is Christ speaking: “And in them is fulfilled the prophecy of Esaias, which saith, By hearing ye shall hear, and shall not understand”: you Israelites, you don’t understand. “And seeing ye shall see, and shall not perceive: For this people’s heart is waxed gross”: that’s what it means to make their heart fat, waxed gross. “And their ears are dull of hearing, and their eyes they have closed; lest at any time they should see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and should understand with their heart, and should be converted, and I should heal them.”

The Lord is letting us know there’s a remnant allotted not to wake up. Some of your mothers, some of your fathers, some of your children will not wake up to this truth. They will fight you; they will come against you.

But you men and women, Christ said, “blessed are your eyes, for they see: and your ears, for they hear.”

Christ said the same thing Isaiah said. Remember what we just read: until the cities be wasted without inhabitant, the houses without man, the land utterly desolate, and the Lord have removed men far away, and a great forsaking in the midst of the land. Watch what Christ says: “And they shall fall by the edge of the sword”: the Israelites that remain would fall by the edge of the sword, Rome’s sword, “and shall be led away captive into all nations”.

“And Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles”: so who’s going to live in Jerusalem? “Until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled”: until the time of the Gentile rulership be fulfilled. So Christ is saying the same thing that Isaiah said.

sense.text:
This is a precept for what we just read in 2 Esdras chapter two, where it said, I will send Isaiah and Jeremiah back. “And thou, even thyself”: thou meaning Jeremiah, even you, Jeremiah, “shalt discontinue from thine heritage that I gave thee”. That’s talking about when he went into slavery, not during that time, but when he would come back. He’s being specific to Jeremiah: you’re going to be discontinued from the heritage that I gave you.

“And I will cause thee to serve thine enemies in the land which thou knowest not”: in America. Jeremiah went on the slave ships. Jeremiah was shackled up beside you and me. That’s prophetic. Remember, Jeremiah never went to Babylon. He came back to the land: Jeremiah was let go, and he went back to Jerusalem. It didn’t happen then. So he’s telling him, you’re going to go serve slavery, Jeremiah.

The prophets are back on the earth. That’s why these churches don’t want to deal with us. They don’t want to sit down and talk with us with this Bible, because they know we are going to pick this Bible apart. To the people in Islam and in the Christian church: it’s time for you to examine who you are learning from. Many of you have a zeal for God, but not according to knowledge. It’s time for you to question that and come home. You are the Israelites.
“And the Lord have removed men far away”: the Lord removed the Israelite men far away, “and there be a great forsaking in the midst of the land.”

“But yet in it shall be a tenth.” Pay close attention to that. This tenth here is more than the one third in America. This tenth is talking about Israel worldwide. Remember, we were scattered; we were removed into all places. God said in Israel there’s going to be a tenth that’s going to come back. So that’s not just America: that’s Africa, that’s Europe, that’s the Caribbean islands, that’s over in the Iran areas. “It” is Israel, “and it shall return”: that tenth shall return to the one true God, “and shall be eaten”.

Look at the imagery: “as a teil tree, and as an oak”. It’s giving you the image of a tree cut down, two trees cut down. Why two trees? Because we’re split into two kingdoms. Can that tree live again? Yeah, because all you need is that one little sprout to come up, and that tree will live again. That’s what he’s saying here.

“Whose substance is in them”: that substance is God’s spirit, the reawakening of God’s spirit that’s in us, “when they cast their leaves: so the holy seed shall be the substance thereof.” The holy seed begins with Christ; that’s the only way that substance can come back.

precepts.why:
We always read this. “And it shall come to pass, that in all the land”: see that word, land. Land, meaning this is about America, the land only, America. “Saith the Lord, two parts therein shall be cut off and die”: two parts of the Israelites here shall be cut off and die. “But the third shall be left therein”, meaning the third is going to repent.

The tenth of Isaiah 6:13 is more than this one third in America: it is Israel worldwide.

The precept for the holy seed. “For they have taken of their daughters for themselves, and for their sons: so that the holy seed have mingled themselves with the people of those lands.” We sinned, and it still refers to us as the holy seed. We are the holy seed. But as we read on, the holy seed begins with Christ.

Here’s an analogy that Job gives about the tree, so you can get the visual. “For there is hope of a tree”: remember, we’re talking about the teil tree and the oak tree, “if it be cut down, that it will sprout again”. Although you cut it down, Job says it’s going to sprout again, “and that the tender branch thereof will not cease.”

God gave the same analogy to Isaiah for us. Although we got destroyed as a nation, as a people, as a race, the substance is still in them; the Holy Spirit is still going to reactivate them, reawaken them.

“Though the root thereof wax old in the earth, and the stock thereof die in the ground; Yet through the scent of water”: the scent of water is God’s word, “it will bud”: you’ll start to grow again. That’s what you’re seeing right now, “and bring forth boughs like a plant.”

“The remnant shall return, even the remnant of Jacob, unto the mighty God.” See that: the remnant shall return. “For though thy people Israel be as the sand of the sea, yet a remnant of them shall return”: that’s that tenth we were just reading about. “The consumption decreed shall overflow with righteousness.”

It’s the same analogy: you’ve got a stump. “And there shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse”: a plant is going to grow out of the stump of Jesse, “and a Branch shall grow out of his roots: And the spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him”. This is talking about Christ. That’s why he’s the first of the holy seed: “the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of the Lord”. Without Christ we would not be here; it had to start with him.

sense.text:
“And the remnant that is escaped of the house of Judah shall again take root downward, and bear fruit upward.” It is the same analogy as the stump of the tree: the nation of Israel was cut down like the stump of a tree, but they are going to grow back. “Shall again take root downward”: this starts with Christ. Without Christ we would not be here; it had to start with him.

That is why it is so important that it says Judah. People want to know why all nations and races can come here, but they are so hard on the so-called American black, so hard on that group right there. Because they know this whole thing is going to start with Judah.

“For out of Jerusalem shall go forth a remnant, and they that escape out of mount Zion: the zeal of the Lord of hosts shall do this.” A remnant goes forth out of Jerusalem, and it is the zeal of the Lord of hosts that does it.

precepts.why:
“And this is the blessing of Judah: and he said, Hear, Lord, the voice of Judah, and bring him unto his people.” The whole thing starts with Judah, and the Lord brings Judah unto his people.

They know that group right there. Like we read in the book that that Edomite wrote, he said that group right there, that group of fake ass Israelites. They don’t want to admit it, but they know it is Judah, and that is why they are so hard on the so-called American black.

sense.text: “I am the true vine, and my Father is the husbandman.” Christ said, I’m the true vine. That goes back to Isaiah 11, the rod out of the stem of Jesse; it goes back to Isaiah 6:13, the holy seed as the substance of the tree. It starts with Christ.

“Every branch in me that beareth not fruit he taketh away”: if you don’t bear fruit in this truth, brothers and sisters, if you want to still be that old scallywag brother, or you want to be that sister who’s a hoe with a w, you’re gonna be taken away. What it means not to bear fruit is spelled out in the works of the flesh (Galatians 5:19-21).

“And every branch that beareth fruit, he purgeth it, that it may bring forth more fruit.” What do you call it when you purge a tree? You prune it. You trim it so you keep it growing, so it can grow right. That’s our trials, that’s our tribulations, that’s our temptations: that’s the purging, the pruning of us. We want that part, the branch that bears fruit, and the fruit is the fruit of the Spirit (Galatians 5:22-23).
“Now ye are clean through the word which I have spoken unto you.” Not water baptism: the word of God is what cleans you.

“Abide in me, and I in you. As the branch cannot bear fruit of itself, except it abide in the vine; no more can ye, except ye abide in me.” That’s why it all starts with Christ. We can’t do nothing without the king.
“I am the vine, ye are the branches: He that abideth in me, and I in him, the same bringeth forth much fruit: for without me ye can do nothing.” Christ is the vine, you are the branches.

precepts.why:
This is what it means when it says “Every branch in me that beareth not fruit he taketh away.” If you don’t bear fruit in this truth, this is what you’re doing: “Now the works of the flesh are manifest, which are these; Adultery, fornication, uncleanness, lasciviousness”. Adultery; fornication, that’s still sexual sin.

Uncleanness: vile affections. That’s you pedophiles. Some of you ain’t touched nobody, but you brothers online looking at child porn, you better correct that.

Lasciviousness is offensive sexual desire. Some of your brothers, some of your sisters too: ‘he got to be 13 inches.’ She ain’t ready to get married; she’s still a hoe with a w.

“Idolatry”: you got your cross around your neck; you got that thing Muslims wear, the crescent moon and the star. It’s all idolatry. “Witchcraft”: you and your horoscopes and all that. “Hatred”: hatred for your brother, for your sister. “Variance”: conflicts. You are always contrary and conflicted with somebody, and some of your brothers know who you are.

“Emulations”: when you imitate for the wrong reason, you emulate to be better than somebody. The disciples imitated Christ, but that was a good thing; they wanted to be like him. Emulation is trying to be better than someone in a negative context.

“Wrath, strife, seditions, heresies, Envyings, murders, drunkenness”: we had to deal with drunkenness a couple of weeks ago. “Revellings” is partyings. Not righteous parties: in the world, at the club, where they say keep it real hot, so that way they buy alcohol and play songs about adultery, so no matter who is married they gonna get together. All that is witchcraft; there’s a science behind it.

That is the branch that bears not fruit, and he takes it away.

sense.text:
This is the fruit of the branch that bears fruit in John 15:2. “But the fruit of the Spirit is love”: not the way the Christian woman and Christian man say, ‘I just love, love.’ The love the Bible is talking about is keeping the commandments (2 John 1:6), and that is the first fruit of the Spirit. These Christians are not keeping the commandments; they’ll associate with everything else in there, but not keep the first one, love, which is the keeping of God’s commandments.

“Joy”: some of y’all are keeping the commandments, but you don’t have no joy in this truth. You’re miserable, ‘oh gosh, I gotta keep’ it, because you hate God’s commandments (Amos 8:5).

“Peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith”. Take moral inventory of yourself, which is self-examination: look at the fruits of the Spirit and the works of the flesh, and identify where you fit in. Everybody here looks like a super Israelite, meanwhile back at the ranch.

“Meekness”: the word meekness goes into humble. Not humble to somebody saying you got to be humble to me; humble to the word of God. Meekness means humble to the word: whatever it says, you’re going to do it (Revelation 14:4).

“Temperance”: discipline yourself. “Against such there is no law.” There’s no law you can pull to condemn any of those fruits of the Spirit, because all those fruits of the Spirit are based on the keeping of God’s commandments. That’s the root of it, in Christ: the root of it, the trunk of it.

precepts.why: “And this is love, that we walk after his commandments. This is the commandment, That, as ye have heard from the beginning, ye should walk in it.” We’re not without understanding the biblical context of the word love. The love the Bible is talking about is keeping the commandments, and that is the first fruit of the Spirit. You can’t knock that out.

You have no joy, you’re miserable, because you hate God’s commandments: “Saying, When will the new moon be gone, that we may sell corn?” When will the new moon be gone, I can’t stand it; I want to sell, I want to do work, I want to do business. “And the sabbath, that we may set forth wheat”: when will that sabbath be gone, I can’t stand that sabbath day. “Making the ephah small, and the shekel great, and falsifying the balances by deceit”.

That is keeping the commandments without the joy that is a fruit of the Spirit.

An example of meekness: “These are they which were not defiled with women; for they are virgins. These are they which follow the Lamb whithersoever he goeth.” They follow Christ wherever he goes. Whatever Christ says do, they do. That is being meek, humble to the word.

sense.text:
“Now to Abraham and his seed were the promises made. He saith not, And to seeds, as of many; but as of one, And to thy seed, which is Christ.” That’s why the holy seed starts with Christ. It does not start with us; it starts with Christ. He is the first of the holy seed, the holy seed Christ, of the tribe of Judah, for Israel.

That’s what Matthew chapter 1, verse 1 all the way down to 16, is all about: it gives you his generations, his genealogy. The holy seed would come through that lineage.

“The burden of Dumah.” Who is Dumah? Dumah is one of the sons of Ishmael (Genesis 25:12-14). These are the Arabs. Even the Zondervan Bible dictionary, under Ishmaelite, says it: ‘All Arabs, following Muhammad’s example, claimed descent from Ishmael.’ The scholars know the Arabs are Ishmael. Y’all didn’t know that was in there.

This is the prophecy concerning Ishmael, the Arabs: what God says is going to happen to them. The Quran ain’t gonna say it, and Sunday school ain’t gonna teach it. Our job is to win our people, the dead Israelites, to this truth, and that is done through teaching, not arguing back and forth. When you read about Christ, he didn’t argue; he gave the scripture and kept it moving.

“He calleth to me out of Seir”: Seir is the range of mountains where Esau used to live. In many of these books you read about the Nabataeans; those Arabs took that whole Mount Seir over.

“Watchman, what of the night? Watchman, what of the night?” Isaiah is the watchman. He asked him twice: the prophet is the watchman.
“The watchman said, The morning cometh, and also the night: if ye will enquire, enquire ye: return, come.”
“The burden upon Arabia.” This is the burden upon the Arabs.

“The inhabitants of the land of Tema”: who is Tema? Tema is a son of Ishmael (Genesis 25:13-15). These are Arabs. “Brought water to him that was thirsty, they prevented with their bread him that fled”: when people fled from war, it was customary to help them in the desert.

“For they fled from the swords, from the drawn sword, and from the bent bow, and from the grievousness of war.” This is letting you know war is coming, and the Arabs would flee from the sword. These wars did happen back then, during the time of Isaiah, but Isaiah is also prophesying about things to come. That is what all of us need to understand. The example of that war is in 2 Esdras 15, the dragons of Arabia.

“For thus hath the Lord said unto me, Within a year, according to the years of an hireling, and all the glory of Kedar shall fail”. Kedar was one of the sons of Ishmael, which means dark skin. All the glory of them Arabs shall fail.

“And the residue of the number of archers, the mighty men of the children of Kedar, shall be diminished”: shall be destroyed. “For the Lord God of Israel hath spoken it.” God prophesied that thing. So we ain’t worried about the Arabs; we’re going to tell you what’s going to happen to the Arabs.

precepts.why:
“Now these are the generations of Ishmael, Abraham’s son, whom Hagar the Egyptian, Sarah’s handmaid, bare unto Abraham: And these are the names of the sons of Ishmael, by their names, according to their generations”, and among them is “Dumah.” Dumah is one of the sons of Ishmael. The burden of Dumah is the burden of Ishmael, and these are the Arabs.

The scripture says prove all things, so here it is proven: the Arabs come from Ishmael. Put that in your pipe and smoke it.

“And these are the names of the sons of Ishmael, by their names, according to their generations: the firstborn of Ishmael, Nebajoth; and Kedar, and Adbeel, and Mibsam, And Mishma, and Dumah, and Massa, Hadar, and Tema”. Tema: that’s Ishmael. The inhabitants of the land of Tema in Isaiah 21:14 are Arabs, and so is Kedar of verse 16.

sense.text: Here is an example of the war Isaiah is talking about, and Ezra goes into detail. “Behold an horrible vision, and the appearance thereof from the east: Where the nations of the dragons of Arabia shall come out with many chariots”. The dragons of what? Of Arabia. The Arabs are going to come out to make war. “And the multitude of them shall be carried as the wind upon earth”: there’s going to be a lot of Arab nations that come to make war, “that all they which hear them may fear and tremble.” Everybody that hears about these Arabs, the sons of Ishmael, shall be afraid.

“Also the Carmanians raging in wrath shall go forth as the wild boars of the wood”: the Carmanians, that’s Iran. Write that down. “And with great power shall they come, and join battle with them, and shall waste a portion of the land of the Assyrians.” When it says the land of the Assyrians, it is talking about modern-day Israel. Remember, when you read the Bible, Assyria took over the northern kingdom, took them out, and put replacement nations there. That’s the same thing they did in 1948: they put other nations there, the Edomite nations (Ezekiel 36:5).

They are going to waste a portion of the land of modern-day Israel. This is why they are so hellbent on Iran not getting uranium for a nuclear bomb. Iran keeps saying we’re going to wipe Israel off the map, and they know the prophecy: don’t let them get uranium, they’ll blow us to kingdom come.

“And then shall the dragons have the upper hand”: the dragons go back to verse 29, the nations of the dragons of Arabia. They have the upper hand because they destroy a portion of the land of Assyria, which is modern-day Israel. “Remembering their nature”: what is their nature? Ishmael, the wild man (Genesis 16:11-12).

“And if they shall turn themselves, conspiring together in great power to persecute them”: they’re going to conspire together and persecute modern Israel.

“Then these shall be troubled”: these Arabs, it says they’re gonna be troubled. “And keep silence through their power, and shall flee.” The Arabs and Iran are gonna flee, because Israel has been built up by America and London. They got the Iron Dome; Israel is like America over there. They got a military power, they got satellites. Them Arab nations can’t roll with that. They might get some of them Israelis, but they ain’t finished yet.

“And from the land of the Assyrians shall the enemy besiege them”: from the land of modern Israel they’re going to besiege the Arabs, besiege Iran, “and consume some of them”, consume some of the Arabs, consume some of Iran. “And in their host shall be fear and dread, and strife among their kings”: their leaders are going to be fussing and fighting.

precepts.why:
This is about Idumea taking the land: “Therefore thus saith the Lord God; Surely in the fire of my jealousy have I spoken against the residue of the heathen, and against all Idumea”. Idumea is the Greek word for Edomite: the Caucasians.

“Which have appointed my land into their possession”: the land of Israel. They took the land, “with the joy of all their heart”, saying, we are Yahudi, we’ll take the land as Jewish. “With despiteful minds”: hateful minds, “to cast it out for a prey.” They said to their fellows, come to Israel, calling them brothers from Poland, Czechoslovakia, Uzbekistan, Russia, Germany, France: come get a piece of this land, it’s a free-for-all. That’s what it means to cast it out for a prey.

So the land of the Assyrians in 2 Esdras 15:30 is that land: modern-day Israel, where the Edomite nations were put in 1948 the way Assyria put replacement nations in the land of the northern kingdom.

What is their nature? “And the angel of the Lord said unto her”, unto Hagar, the mother, “Behold, thou art with child, and shalt bear a son, and shalt call his name Ishmael”. These are the Arabs; this is the forefather of the Arab race. “Because the Lord hath heard thy affliction”: the word Ishmael means affliction heard.

“And he will be a wild man”: the Bible prophesies that the Arabs would be a wild man. How wild, you ask? So wild they will strap C4 on their chest and blow everybody to hell and back, thinking they’re going to get 70 virgins in heaven. And it’s always the young ones: they tell them, we’ll give your family money, but we want you to go out there and kill everybody, and you’re going to get 70 virgins. Why doesn’t one of them say, why don’t that old dude go, he about to go anyway? It never happens.

“His hand will be against every man, and every man’s hand against him”: that’s letting you know, the Arabs are for themselves. That’s to you Muslim brothers and sisters out there: they’re not for you, black and Latinos; they’re for themselves. “And he shall dwell in the presence of all his brethren”: that’s that area they call today the Middle East.

That is the nature the dragons of Arabia remember when they have the upper hand.

sense.text:
It looked like we’re done. It looks like the Israelites are finished, but we’re not finished; we’re like that stump growing. “Moreover the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah, saying, Considerest thou not what this people have spoken, saying, The two families which the Lord hath chosen, he hath even cast them off?” God did cast off the two families: the southern kingdom and the northern kingdom.

“Thus they have despised my people, that they should be no more a nation before them.” That’s what happened: we were no more a nation; we were destroyed and scattered worldwide (Romans 11:1).

“Thus saith the Lord; If my covenant be not with day and night”: do we have day and night today? Yes. “And if I have not appointed the ordinances of heaven and earth”: the sun, moon and stars. “Then will I cast away the seed of Jacob”. If you could do away with day and night and the ordinances of heaven and earth, then will I cast away the seed of Jacob. That’s us.

“For I will cause their captivity to return, and have mercy on them.” God is going to cause that captivity to return, bring them back, and God will have mercy on us. And he shows it in an illustration (Hosea 12:10), the similitudes of the prophets.

precepts.why: “I have also spoken by the prophets, and I have multiplied visions, and used similitudes, by the ministry of the prophets.” He used similitudes: one thing he says could mean something else. This is a spiritual book. The return of the captivity in Jeremiah 33 is shown in the similitudes the prophets gave: the tree that sprouts again, the two staves, the two sticks.

Romans 11 goes with what we just read in Jeremiah 33. Paul had to address it: was Israel done away with? “I say then, Hath God cast away his people?” Because that’s what it looked like: God destroyed the twelve tribes of Israel. “God forbid.” Paul said, in the spirit of Christ, no. “For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.”

sense.text:
Here are the similitudes the prophets gave. Remember what Isaiah said, that we would be like the teil tree and the oak tree that would begin to sprout. “And I will feed the flock of slaughter, even you, O poor of the flock.” We’re the flock of slaughter.

“And I took unto me two staves”: staves are two pieces of wood. “The one I called Beauty, and the other I called Bands; and I fed the flock.” These two sticks represent the two kingdoms, Judah and Israel.

“Three shepherds also I cut off in one month”: these are your scribes, your Pharisees and Sadducees, and the elders of Israel (Mark 8:31). “And my soul lothed them”: God said, I hated them. “And their soul also abhorred me”: their soul hated God, hated Christ.

“Then said I, I will not feed you: that that dieth, let it die; and that that is to be cut off, let it be cut off; and let the rest eat every one the flesh of another.” That is cannibalism, in 70 A.D.
“And I took my staff, even Beauty”: that’s the kingdom of Judah. “And cut it asunder, that I might break my covenant which I had made with all the people.”

“And it was broken in that day: and so the poor of the flock that waited upon me knew that it was the word of the Lord.” The poor of the flock that waited upon him are the elect: those were the twelve. When they saw Israel getting jacked up, they knew it was of the Lord.

“And I said unto them, If ye think good, give me my price; and if not, forbear. So they weighed for my price thirty pieces of silver.” That is the price Judas took to betray the Son of God (Matthew 26:15).

“And the Lord said unto me, Cast it unto the potter: a goodly price that I was prised at of them. And I took the thirty pieces of silver, and cast them to the potter in the house of the Lord.” That is what Judas did with the thirty pieces of silver (Matthew 27:5-10).

“Then I cut asunder mine other staff”: the other staff is the northern kingdom, “even Bands, that I might break the brotherhood between Judah and Israel.” That was a prophecy. Notice he used two sticks, two staves, and the same two sticks come together again in Ezekiel 37.

precepts.why: The three shepherds: “And he began to teach them, that the Son of man must suffer many things, and be rejected of the elders, and of the chief priests, and scribes”. These are your scribes, these are your Pharisees, Sadducees and the elders of Israel. That’s who the three shepherds are, cut off in one month, whose soul abhorred God and hated Christ.

“And said unto them, What will ye give me, and I will deliver him unto you?” Judas speaking. “And they covenanted with him for thirty pieces of silver”: they covenanted with Judas for thirty pieces of silver to betray the Son of God. That is the price weighed in Zechariah 11:12.

Some of you in here are not in this truth to win it; you’re in this truth to destroy. Some of you have covenanted with Christian groups, you have covenanted with certain government groups, to try to undo what God is doing here, for thirty pieces. Enjoy your money while it lasts.

What Judas did with the thirty pieces of silver: “And he cast down the pieces of silver in the temple, and departed, and went and hanged himself. And the chief priests took the silver pieces, and said, It is not lawful for to put them into the treasury, because it is the price of blood. And they took counsel, and bought with them the potter’s field, to bury strangers in. Wherefore that field was called, The field of blood, unto this day.” Blood money.

“Then was fulfilled that which was spoken by Jeremy the prophet, saying, And they took the thirty pieces of silver, the price of him that was valued”. It says Jeremy because Zechariah’s prophecies came from Jeremiah originally; but remember, Jeremiah’s books were burnt up. “Whom they of the children of Israel did value; And gave them for the potter’s field, as the Lord appointed me.” That is the casting of the thirty pieces to the potter in the house of the Lord, in Zechariah 11:13.

He used two staves to break the brotherhood between Judah and Israel. Now Ezekiel uses the word stick: “Moreover, thou son of man, take thee one stick, and write upon it, For Judah, and for the children of Israel his companions”. Judah and his companions: that’s Levi and Benjamin. “Then take another stick, and write upon it, For Joseph, the stick of Ephraim, and for all the house of Israel his companions”: Joseph, which is in the hand of Ephraim, and his companions, Simeon, Issachar, Zebulun, and so forth and so on.

“And join them one to another into one stick; and they shall become one in thine hand.” The sticks that were cut asunder are put back together. “And when the children of thy people shall speak unto thee, saying, Wilt thou not shew us what thou meanest by these?” When the Israelites see that, they’re going to ask what you mean by this. This is where we get the twelve tribes sign: why do you have those tribes together on that sign? This is where we get it from.

sense.text: It’s the same thing in the New Testament: the two sticks coming together. They thought this was the end of our people. It’s not the end; this is only just beginning. “For if the firstfruit be holy, the lump is also holy: and if the root be holy, so are the branches.” Who’s the root? Christ is that root. And who are the branches? Israel is the branches.

“And if some of the branches be broken off”: why does it say olive tree? Because the Lord called Israel a green olive tree, and the branches of it are broken (Jeremiah 11:16-17). “And thou, being a wild olive tree”: the wild olive tree was Israel, meaning the northern kingdom. “Wert graffed in among them”. This is saying the same thing Ezekiel was saying. This ain’t about Esau being grafted in, or the Chinese being grafted in. It is Israel, the two kingdoms.

“And with them partakest of the root and fatness of the olive tree”: the root is Christ, and the fatness is the blessings of the olive tree. God called us an olive tree.

“Boast not against the branches.” He’s telling the Israelites of the northern kingdom: brothers, don’t boast against the branches. “But if thou boast, thou bearest not the root, but the root thee.” You don’t bear Christ; Christ, the root, is the one that allows you to be grafted back into this truth.

“Thou wilt say then, The branches were broken off, that I might be graffed in.” They fell: the southern kingdom, them wicked scribes and Pharisees, who God killed. They were broken off that we might be grafted in. “Well; because of unbelief they were broken off”: they were only broken off because they didn’t believe. “And thou standest by faith. Be not highminded, but fear”.
“For if God spared not the natural branches”: the natural branches were the southern kingdom of Judah. He came to them first. “Take heed lest he also spare not thee.”

“Behold therefore the goodness and severity of God: on them which fell, severity”. He was severe with Judah. Remember what Paul said: since you put it from you, we turn to the Gentiles. He turned to the northern kingdom. “But toward thee, goodness, if thou continue in his goodness”. What is God’s goodness? The law and the commandment (Romans 7:12). So continuing in his goodness is continuing in the commandments. “Otherwise thou also shalt be cut off.”

“And they also”: they also of Judah, “if they abide not still in unbelief”, if they repent and get themselves together, “shall be graffed in: for God is able to graff them in again.” The key word is again. This ain’t talking about the Philistines and the Jebusites; they were never in this.

“For if thou wert cut out of the olive tree which is wild by nature”: all Israel is called the olive tree. Wild by nature means we were wicked as hell, sinful, into idolatry, breaking all God’s laws. “And wert graffed contrary to nature into a good olive tree”: through Christ they got a chance to repent and get themselves right. “How much more shall these, which be the natural branches”: how much more Judah, which be the natural branches, “be graffed into their own olive tree?” All Israel’s coming back together.

“For I would not, brethren, that ye should be ignorant of this mystery”. This was a mystery, brothers and sisters: that God would destroy the twelve tribes of Israel and bring them back together in the last days. “Lest ye should be wise in your own conceits; that blindness in part is happened to Israel, until the fulness of the Gentiles be come in.”

Here’s the key: “And so all Israel shall be saved”. If you ever want to know what Romans 11 is talking about, start with verse 26 and then go back. It lets you know what the whole chapter is about: all Israel, the twelve tribes of Israel. That’s what the grafting in is about: Christ, and bringing all the twelve tribes back together again.

“As it is written, There shall come out of Sion the Deliverer”: the deliverer is Christ, who the world calls Jesus the Christ. “And shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob”. He’s not turning away ungodliness from the Jebusites, the Philistines or the Egyptians; he’s turning away ungodliness from Jacob, from the twelve tribes of Israel.
“For this is my covenant unto them”: them who? Them Israelites. “When I shall take away their sins.” This whole thing is about Israel (Hebrews 8:8).

precepts.why:
Why does it say olive tree? “The Lord called thy name, A green olive tree, fair, and of goodly fruit: with the noise of a great tumult he hath kindled fire upon it, and the branches of it are broken.” God called Israel an olive tree, and the branches of it are broken.

“For the Lord of hosts, that planted thee, hath pronounced evil against thee, for the evil of the house of Israel and of the house of Judah, which they have done against themselves to provoke me to anger in offering incense unto Baal.” Both houses, Israel and Judah, are that olive tree, and both were broken for their evil. So the branches broken off and the wild olive tree grafted in, in Romans 11, are Israel and Judah: the two kingdoms.

What is God’s goodness, brothers? “Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good.” The commandment is good. So when Romans 11:22 says “if thou continue in his goodness”, that goodness is continuing in the commandments; otherwise thou also shalt be cut off.

“Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah”. The covenant of Romans 11:27, “this is my covenant unto them”, is with the house of Israel and the house of Judah. This whole thing, brothers and sisters, is about Israel: the twelve tribes.
